🇲🇽📊 <u>Delfina Holds 67% in the State of Mexico</u>

Delfina Gómez, the first woman ever to govern the State of Mexico, sits at 67.1% approval (Demoscopia Digital, April 2026) — among the highest of any governor in the country — three years after prying the nation's most populous state from more than nine decades of PRI rule. Voters credit her social programs, above all "Mujeres con Bienestar," which puts support directly in the hands of the most vulnerable.

🇲🇽🤝 <u>Welfare Up, Deficit Down</u>

Mexico's 2027 budget is a direct answer to the "social spending equals fiscal ruin" script: more than 1 trillion pesos for welfare — 543.5 billion for the universal elderly pension, 190.6 billion for Benito Juárez scholarships, 133.6 billion for the Rita Cetina scholarship — "protection from childhood to old age." It does it while cutting the deficit to 3.4% of GDP, a cumulative 1.8-point drop since 2024, and running a primary surplus, with "no new taxes for the people, no gasolinazos," said Sheinbaum.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Ayotzinapa: New Evidence Before the 12th Anniversary</u>

Ahead of the September 26 twelfth anniversary of the disappearance of the 43 Ayotzinapa students, the Sheinbaum government is readying a fresh report with new evidence and lines of investigation, coordinated by Attorney General Ernestina Godoy and special prosecutor Mauricio Pazarán. Interior Secretary Rosa Icela Rodríguez says the new leads have already produced arrests of figures never touched before — among them former Guerrero governor Ángel Aguirre, accused of concealing recordings from the night of the crime.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Another US-Made Arsenal Turns Up in Culiacán</u>

In Culiacán, the Army and state police raided two homes on a private road in Isla Musalá — meters from the residence of Governor Rubén Rocha Moya — seizing automatic rifles, magazines, cartridges, tactical gear and at least seven vehicles after an anonymous emergency call. The haul fits the pattern Mexico keeps putting on the table: roughly 80% of the guns recovered at its crime scenes are trafficked south from the United States.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>The Azcatitlan Codex Comes Home</u>

For the first time in some 200 years, the Codex Azcatitlan — the Mexica pictorial manuscript that charts the migration from Aztlán to the founding of Tenochtitlan and the line of its rulers — returns to Mexican soil, on display at the National Museum of Anthropology from Sept 17. Held all this time in France's Bibliothèque nationale, it crosses back as part of the Mexico–France bicentennial, with Mexico lending the Códice Boturini in return. "There is no prosperity without recognizing history," said Sheinbaum.
📸 Honestidad y resultados en Hidalgo — Pachuca de Soto, 13 de septiembre de 2026

🇲🇽✊ "The welfare programs are love turned into policy." An ex-president called the seniors' pension "supporting the lazy." Sheinbaum's answer: our elders are heroes and heroines of the homeland. — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Hidalgo In Hidalgo alone, 358,297 seniors receive the universal pension — a constitutional right that rises with inflation every year.

🇲🇽🌎 A U.S. president testified to Mexican courage. Sheinbaum read it back. "I have never seen soldiers as brave as the Mexicans — how they fought to defend their homeland." — Ulysses S. Grant, quoted by President Sheinbaum in Hidalgo The U.S. invasion of 1846–48 took more than half of Mexico's territory. Grant, who fought in that war and later became president, called it deeply unjust.

🇲🇽✊ "When you support those who have the least, the whole country does better." Over 1.1 million people in Hidalgo — more than a third of the state's families — receive direct government support through the Banco del Bienestar, with no intermediaries. — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Hidalgo "For the good of all, first the poor" — the humanist model funded, she said, by rooting out corruption.

🇲🇽🏭 Minimum wage up 154% in real terms in 8 years — and no inflation. For 36 years they warned that raising the minimum wage would bring inflation, devalue the peso, and scare off investment. None of it happened. — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Hidalgo The peso is among the world's strongest currencies and Mexico is at a record for foreign direct investment.
